MINUTES
  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING
  MAY 8, 2019

1.  CALL TO ORDER

  CHAIR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

  Committee Members Present:  Chair Schmitz, Pope, Boothe, Martin, Munday,
  Scott

  Committee Members Absent:  Combs, Lum, Retz, Vanden Bos

  Staff Members Present:  Greg Grammer, Assistant City Manager
  David Wahba, Planning Director
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy, Willdan
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  Also Present:  Investigator Johann Schloegle, LACSD
  Deputy Tami Bouse, LACSD

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  COMMITTEE MEMBER MARTIN, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY made
  a motion to,

  APPROVE MINUTES OF THE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING
  OF February 20, 2019 AS PRESENTED.

  AYES:  Schmitz, Pope, Boothe, Martin, Munday
  NOES:
  ABSENT:  Combs, Lum, Vanden Bos
  ABSTAIN:  Scott

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

  None

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  777 SILVER SPUR ROAD AT ROXCOVE DRIVE – CONSIDERATION OF RED CURB
  REMOVAL
  Assistant to the City Manager Grammer stated that this item was a request from a resident
  on behalf of a business owner at 777 Silver Spur Road who asked that the length of the
  red curb in front of this business be reduced.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a summary of the staff report and stated that
  there is red curb in front of 777 Silver Spur Road and to the east, across Roxcove Drive.
  She reviewed the site and found that drivers turning from Roxcove Drive and looking at
  eastbound traffic provided visibility of approximately 400 ft. and drivers turning and looking
  at westbound traffic had visibility of approximately 350 ft.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that, based on the analysis of Silver Spur Road
  at Roxcove Drive, the recommendation is to remove 85 feet of red curb on the south curb
  line of Silver Spur Road starting from approximately 80 feet west of Roxcove Drive; and
  to install a “2-hour parking 7am to 6pm Except Sundays” sign, on the south side of Silver
  Spur Road at approximately 80 feet west of Roxcove Drive.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ asked if the red curb on the curved portion of the Silver Spur to Roxcove
  will be removed and expressed concern with the visibility when vehicles are actually
  parked in the portion that will be removed. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that

   the red curb in front of 777 Silver Spur Road closest to Roxcove will not be removed and
  stated that she is confident that the removal of the red curb will not be noticeable.

  In response to a question by CHAIR SCHMITZ, Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated
  that the 2-hour parking sign will go (approximately 80 feet) from Roxcove Drive on Silver
  Spur Road and extends the existing 2-hour parking zone in this area of Silver Sur Road.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY to,

  REMOVE 85 FT. OF RED CURB ON THE SOUTH CURB LINE OF SILVER SPUR
  ROAD STARTING FROM APPROXIMATELY 80 FT. WEST OF ROXCOVE
  DRIVE; AND TO INSTALL A, “2-HOUR PARKING 7AM TO 6PM EXCEPT
  SUNDAYS” SIGN, ON THE SOUTH SIDE OF SILVER SPUR ROAD AT
  APPROXIMATELY 80 FT. WEST OF ROXCOVE DRIVE.

  AYES:  Schmitz, Pope, Boothe, Martin, Munday, Scott
  NOES:
  ABSENT:  Combs, Lum, Vanden Bos
  ABSTAIN:

B.  SILVER SPUR ROAD AND RANGE HORSE LANE – CONSIDERATION OF
  ADDITIONAL TRAFFIC CONTROLS

  Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that staff was contacted by residents on Range
  Horse Lane, who had concerns with traffic at Silver Spur Road and Range Horse Lane
  and the number of accidents at the guardrail. In particular, they asked if the guardrail could
  be extended and to keep vehicles travelling in their respective lane.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a summary of the staff report and stated that
  consideration was given to extending the guardrail towards Range Horse Lane. She stated
  that some of the guardrail may have been removed during the design of the pedestrian
  crossing and the handicap ramp, but believes that the guardrail could be extended without
  impacting these areas. While observing the site, there were vehicles crossing the center
  line markers and placing more raised reflective pavement markers across the center line
  will help this issue and provide more visibility at night. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki
  stated that the collision history showed that there were four accidents reported between
  January 2012 and December 2018, and three of the four accidents were due to inattention.
  Reflective markers on the guardrail is being proposed to draw attention to the guardrail.
  Lastly, in looking at the curve and the speed in which vehicles are travelling, there is a
  need to add three chevron signs at 120 ft. apart.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that based on the analysis of Silver Spur
  Road in the vicinity of Range Horse Lane, the following is recommended: Extend the
  guardrail approximately 25 feet north, towards Range Horse Lane; Add raised
  reflective pavement markers (RPMs) on the yellow centerline striping every 12 feet
  from the entrance driveway of Ascension Church to approximately 200 feet north of
  Range Horse Lane (approximately 410 feet total striping); Install white reflective
  markers on the top of every other post of the guardrail (approximately 12 feet
  spacing) from Range Horse Lane to the exit driveway of Ascension Church
  (approximately 350 feet of guardrail); and, Install three (3) additional sets (facing both
  directions of travel) of chevron signs (W1-8) at approximately120 foot spacing as
  shown on Exhibit B of the staff report.

  In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT, Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Itagaki stated that the in the three accidents mentioned the vehicles were driving uphill.

  Deputy Bouse stated the four accidents are those that were reported and more accidents
  may have occurred. There is no requirement that all accidents be reported.

  A discussion ensued on the placement of reflectors and chevron signs.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that there has been concern with the length of
  the pedestrian crossing and this could be reviewed in the future.

   COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT asked about adding one additional chevron to alert
  people of the beginning of the curve. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that she
  would like to review this prior to making any recommendation.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ expressed her concern with the amount of traffic controls being
  proposed and how it can dilute the power of the signs.

  In response to a comment by COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE, Traffic Engineering
  Deputy Itagaki clarified that the proposed pavement markers will be the same as the
  markers currently existing on the double yellow striping.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
  BOOTHE to,

  EXTEND THE GUARDRAIL APPROXIMATELY 25 FEET NORTH, TOWARDS
  RANGE HORSE LANE; ADD RAISED REFLECTIVE PAVEMENT MARKERS
  (RPMS) ON THE YELLOW CENTERLINE STRIPING EVERY 12 FEET FROM
  THE ENTRANCE DRIVEWAY OF ASCENSION CHURCH TO
  APPROXIMATELY 200 FEET NORTH OF RANGE HORSE LANE
  (APPROXIMATELY 410 FEET TOTAL STRIPING); INSTALL WHITE
  REFLECTIVE MARKERS ON THE TOP OF EVERY OTHER POST OF THE
  GUARDRAIL (APPROXIMATELY 12 FEET SPACING) FROM RANGE
  HORSE LANE TO THE EXIT DRIVEWAY OF ASCENSION CHURCH
  (APPROXIMATELY 350 FEET OF GUARDRAIL); AND, INSTALL THREE (3)
  ADDITIONAL SETS OF CHEVRON SIGNS (W1-8) AT APPROXIMATELY 120
  FOOT SPACING AS SHOWN ON EXHIBIT B OF THE STAFF REPORT.

  AYES:  Schmitz, Pope, Boothe, Martin, Munday, Scott
  NOES:
  ABSENT:  Combs, Lum, Vanden Bos
  ABSTAIN:

6.  DIRECTOR’S ITEMS

  Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that at the last meeting COMMITTEE MEMBER
  BOOTHE expressed a concern with the Stop sign eastbound at Palos Verdes Drive North
  making a right on Silver Spur Road.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that there was thought of changing the Stop sign
  to a Yield sign. She stated that it has always been a stop sign and due to the way the
  crossing is there, it would be best to keep it a stop sign.

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE, CHAIR SCHMITZ stated
  that items discussed where no decision is made, the item is set aside unless there is a
  need to revisit it.
  COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE asked about the bike lane on Palos Verdes Drive East
  adjacent to the Rolling Hills Country Club. Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that
  Willdan will be preparing a proposal in the near future for the design and construction of
  possible bike lanes and pedestrian improvements and on Palos Verdes Drive East and on
  Rolling Hills Road. Funding for these projects may be available through grant
  opportunities. CHAIR SCHMITZ added that Lomita will be doing work on their bike lane
  on Narbonne Avenue and the City may be able to link to that project.
  In response to a question from COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE, CHAIR SCHMITZ
  suggested that a list of items for review by the Committee can be included as part of the
  Traffic and Safety Committee agenda.
  DEPUTY BOUSE asked about the portion of the walking trail that has been closed on
  Palos Verdes Drive East adjacent to the Rolling Hills Country Club. Planning Director
  Wahba stated that the storm drained failed in that area and there should be a more
  definitive direction on who is responsible for the cost of repair and ideally it will be re-
  opened by summer.

   COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT asked if power scooters are legally allowed to be driven
  in the direction of opposing traffic. Deputy Bouse stated that she will look into this and will
  provide the information to staff to forward to the Committee.
  COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT expressed his concern with adding a bike lane due to the
  choke point on Palos Verdes Drive East at the bottom of the golf course.
  COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE expressed her concern with exiting the Masongate
  neighborhood as well as other neighborhoods in the case of an emergency. She also
  expressed concern with the amount of brush on Hawthorne Blvd. Assistant City Manager
  Grammer stated that the City is working with Bennett landscaping on abatement. He also
  stated that the concern about exits will be reviewed.
  COMMITTEE MEMBER POPE stated that the fire department provided a presentation to
  their HOA; a presentation for the entire community may be helpful in order to reassure the
  community on their plan during an emergency.
8.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting at 6:56 p.m. to the next Traffic and Safety
  Committee meeting on Wednesday, August 14, 2019 at 6:00 p.m.
